intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city lights to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while experiencing Iceland's dramatic dark landscapes.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by black lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel, and one silica mud mask.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (to avoid crowds) or Evening (for potential aurora views in winter)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891. Far less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural setting, offering an authentic local bathing experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local fish markets while learning about Viking heritage and modern Icelandic culture.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the fissure make this one of the world's most unique underwater experiences. Dry suits are provided, making it accessible even in cold temperatures.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect baggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. If skies are clear, step outside briefly to scan for the Northern Lights from the resort grounds - January nights in Iceland offer excellent aurora viewing windows.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick budget-friendly snack from a 24-hour petrol station or airport kiosk upon arrival (Skyr yogurt, sandwich, or hot dog - Iceland's famous pylsur hot dogs are around 600 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means near-total darkness, freezing temperatures (avg -1°C to 4°C), and potential snow or ice. Pack warm layers, waterproof boots, and gloves. Download the Veður app (Icelandic Met Office) for weather forecasts and the Aurora Forecast app to track Northern Lights activity. Exchange some currency or ensure your card works internationally.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a light breakfast at the resort. Once rested, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to soak in the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery. Sunrise in January is around 11:00 AM, so there is no rush. Explore the immediate surroundings and take photos of the rugged lava fields and ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Reykjanes Peninsula for a self-guided exploration of the dramatic volcanic landscape. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free entry), a small footbridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet. Walk across and take photos of the rift valley. Nearby, explore the Reykjanes Geopark lava fields on foot - completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and head into the nearest town for dinner. Spend the evening watching for Northern Lights from the resort beach or a dark area nearby. January darkness begins around 4:00 PM, giving long windows for aurora hunting. Check aurora forecast before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Pick up groceries at a nearby Bonus or Kronan supermarket (Iceland's cheapest supermarkets). Skyr, bread, and fruit for a budget breakfast under 500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich from the supermarket to eat on the Reykjanes Peninsula - saves money and time.
meals.dinner: Visit a local petrol station (N1 or Orkan) for Iceland's famous lamb soup (kjötsúpa) or a hot dog (pylsur) - budget-friendly at around 600-1,200 ISK total.

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on groceries at Bonus supermarket today - it's the cheapest chain in Iceland and will save significant money throughout the trip. Buy bread, Skyr, instant oatmeal, eggs, pasta, and snacks for the week. January daylight is only about 5-6 hours, so plan outdoor activities around the brief daylight window (roughly 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM).

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to Reykjavik (approximately 45-50 minutes from Keflavik area). Explore the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church - the exterior and surrounding Skólavörðustígur street are free to visit. Climb the tower for panoramic views of Reykjavik (small fee around 1,000 ISK). Walk down to Harpa Concert Hall and admire the stunning geometric glass facade from outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik's colorful old town (Tjörnin lake area) for free. Walk around the city pond and watch the Arctic birds. Visit Landnámssýningin - The Settlement Exhibition (around 1,800 ISK) to learn about Iceland's Viking history. Browse the flea market at Kolaportið if it's open (weekends only, free entry, cheap local goods and food).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Laugavegur, Reykjavik's main shopping street, window shopping and people-watching. Head to a local hot dog stand (Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur - the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland) for a cheap dinner. Return to the resort. Check aurora forecast and head out to a dark spot near the resort for Northern Lights viewing if KP index is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort with groceries purchased yesterday (oatmeal or Skyr with fruit).
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch at Hlöllabátar (Icelandic sub sandwiches, around 1,500-2,000 ISK) or a supermarket deli in Reykjavik.
meals.dinner: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dogs (600-800 ISK each) - an iconic Reykjavik experience on a budget.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is easily walkable. Wear sturdy waterproof boots as January streets can be icy. The Strætó bus system connects Reykjavik to Keflavik (Bus 55, around 2,000 ISK one way) if you don't have a rental car. Consider renting a car for the trip - splitting costs with fellow travelers can make it very budget-friendly and opens up access to remote aurora spots.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the famous Golden Circle route (self-drive or budget tour). First stop: Þingvellir National Park (Thingvellir) - free entry. Walk the rift valley between tectonic plates, visit the Öxará river, and explore the historic site of the world's first parliament (Alþing, established 930 AD). Allow 1.5-2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to Geysir Geothermal Area (free entry). Watch the Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting boiling water 20-30 meters into the air. Walk the geothermal field and observe bubbling mud pools and steaming vents. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall (free entry) - one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort. Stop at a roadside viewpoint for Northern Lights watching if conditions are favorable. The rural areas along the Golden Circle route offer very dark skies perfect for aurora viewing. Return to resort for a self-cooked dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort before departing early.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the supermarket to eat at Geysir or Gullfoss parking area - saves 2,000-3,000 ISK compared to tourist cafes.
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or rice dish at the resort kitchen - budget around 500-800 ISK for ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Roads in January can be icy and snow-covered - check road.is (Icelandic Road Administration website) before departing. Drive slowly and carefully. If renting a car, ensure it has winter tires (mandatory in Iceland October-April). Budget tour operators like Reykjavik Excursions offer Golden Circle tours from around 8,000-10,000 ISK if you prefer not to self-drive.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon area (exterior and surrounding lava fields are free to explore). Note: Entry to the Blue Lagoon itself is expensive (around 9,000-15,000 ISK) and requires advance booking - consider this a splurge day or skip the interior. Instead, explore the dramatic black lava fields surrounding the facility for free. Alternatively, visit the nearby Grindavík fishing village for a glimpse of authentic Icelandic life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seltún Geothermal Area in the Krýsuvík area (free entry) - a stunning landscape of colorful boiling mud pools, steaming vents, and sulfur deposits with vivid yellow, red, and orange hues. Walk the marked boardwalk paths through this otherworldly landscape. Nearby Lake Kleifarvatn is also worth a short stop for dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. This evening, dedicate 2-3 hours specifically to Northern Lights hunting. Drive 10-15 minutes from any light pollution, turn off your car headlights, and let your eyes adjust for 15-20 minutes. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate or tea, warm blankets, and a tripod for long-exposure aurora photography if interested.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from resort for the geothermal area visit.
meals.dinner: Try Grindavík's local fish and chips or visit a petrol station for a budget meal (around 1,000-1,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Seltún is one of Iceland's most underrated and completely free geothermal attractions - far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon area. The sulfur smell is strong but the landscape is extraordinary. Wear shoes you don't mind getting sulfur on. January KP index forecasts of 3 or above give good Northern Lights viewing chances - check en.vedur.is for aurora forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjanesviti, Iceland's oldest lighthouse (free), located on the dramatic Reykjanes Peninsula tip. Walk along the rugged coastline and observe the powerful Atlantic waves crashing against lava cliffs. Nearby, visit the Valahnúkamöl cliffs for spectacular ocean views and birdwatching (gannets and other seabirds). The raw, windswept landscape is quintessentially Icelandic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Eldvörp crater row (free) - a series of small volcanic craters stretching across the Reykjanes lava field. Walk along the marked path between craters for a surreal volcanic landscape experience. Visit the nearby Svartsengi geothermal power plant viewpoint (exterior, free) to see Iceland's sustainable energy infrastructure in action.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Cook a proper meal in the resort kitchen. If weather permits and aurora forecast is good (check app), head to the Reykjanes Peninsula coast for Northern Lights viewing away from light pollution. The coastal dark skies here are excellent for aurora hunting.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Reykjanesviti lighthouse area.
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty meal at resort - try making Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) with ingredients from Bonus supermarket, budget around 800-1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is extremely windy, especially at the lighthouse tip. Dress in full windproof and waterproof gear. This area has seen significant volcanic activity in recent years - check for any active eruption alerts on vedur.is before visiting. If there is a lava eruption occurring nearby, it can be safely viewed from designated areas and provides its own dramatic light show.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Selfoss and the South Coast. Drive east along Route 1 (Ring Road) toward Selfoss town. Stop at Ölfusá river bridge for views. In Selfoss, visit the local market and explore the charming town center. Pick up any supplies needed at the local supermarket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free, small parking fee around 700 ISK). In winter, the waterfall may be partially frozen creating spectacular ice formations. You can walk behind the waterfall (may be closed in icy conditions - check on arrival). Then visit Skógafoss waterfall (free) - another iconic massive waterfall, often with ice and frost formations in January.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward the resort. The South Coast drive offers excellent dark sky viewing - if aurora forecast is favorable, pull over at any safe roadside area for Northern Lights watching. Return to resort for a late self-catered dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort before early departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch to eat near Seljalandsfoss or Skógafoss.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort, or stop at a petrol station on the way back for a budget hot meal.

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 200 km round trip from the Keflavik area. Road conditions in January can be challenging - always check road.is before departing. Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall is often closed in winter due to ice - do not attempt if closed. Skógafoss is accessible year-round. This is a long driving day so start as early as possible to maximize the limited daylight hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Take a long walk along the beachfront in the late morning (around the 11:00 AM sunrise). Collect interesting volcanic rocks and observe the dramatic winter seascape. Spend time reviewing photos from the week and planning the remaining days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal public swimming pool (sundlaug) - Iceland's public pools are heated by geothermal energy and are a beloved local institution. Entry is typically around 1,000-1,200 ISK. Laugardalslaug in Reykjavik is the largest, or find a smaller local pool near the resort. Soak in the hot tubs (heitur pottur), swim in the heated outdoor pools, and experience this authentic Icelandic tradition.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Cook dinner and spend the evening relaxing. If aurora forecast shows high activity (KP 4+), set an alarm for 10:00 PM - 2:00 AM for the best aurora viewing window and head to a dark coastal spot near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered leisurely breakfast - try making Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with ingredients from Bonus.
meals.lunch: Self-catered lunch at resort.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget dinner - try Aktu Taktu burger chain in Reykjavik (around 1,500-2,000 ISK) or self-catered.

day_by_day.notes: Public geothermal pools are one of Iceland's best budget experiences - locals use them daily for socializing. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip flops. Showering without a swimsuit before entering the pool is mandatory by Icelandic custom. The hot pots (hot tubs) range from 38-44°C and are incredibly relaxing, especially in cold January air.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Hafnarfjörður area (just south of Reykjavik, about 30 minutes from Keflavik). This charming town is known for its Viking heritage and alleged hidden people (Huldufólk - elves and hidden beings). Walk the Hellisgerði lava park (free) - a beautiful park built around ancient lava formations where elves are said to live according to Icelandic folklore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hafnarfjörður Museum (small fee, around 1,000 ISK) to learn about local history and the Viking heritage. Explore the town's colorful harbor and watch fishing boats. Walk along the waterfront and visit the Viking Village area. Browse local craft shops along the main street (no obligation to buy).
day_by_day.evening: Head to a dark area near Hafnarfjörður or back toward the Reykjanes Peninsula for Northern Lights hunting. The areas south of Reykjavik have less light pollution than the city itself. Return to resort for self-catered dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Try the fish market in Hafnarfjörður for fresh local fish at reasonable prices, or pack lunch from resort.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort.

day_by_day.notes: Hafnarfjörður is a great alternative to central Reykjavik - similar attractions with fewer tourists and lower prices. The Hellisgerði lava park is particularly atmospheric in winter with snow and ice. Iceland's belief in hidden people (Huldufólk) is genuine - surveys show a significant portion of Icelanders believe in or won't rule out their existence.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (a full day excursion, approximately 2-3 hours drive from Keflavik area). Start early to maximize daylight. Drive north along Route 54 to the peninsula. First stop: Kirkjufell mountain (free) - Iceland's most photographed mountain, especially stunning in winter with snow and often visible alongside the Northern Lights in evening shots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Snæfellsnes Peninsula to Snæfellsjökull National Park (free entry). Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free) with dramatic sea stacks and rusted shipwreck remains. Explore Dritvík cove and lift the ancient strength-testing stones (lyfsteinar) that Viking-era fishermen used to prove their worth. Visit Arnarstapi coastal cliffs (free) with dramatic basalt formations and seabird colonies.
day_by_day.evening: Begin drive back toward the resort. Stop at a roadside viewpoint for Northern Lights watching if conditions are favorable - the Snæfellsnes Peninsula offers exceptionally dark skies. Arrive back at resort late evening. Grab a quick self-catered dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Djúpalónssandur or Arnarstapi.
meals.dinner: Self-catered late dinner at resort, or petrol station stop on the way back.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip (approximately 400 km round trip). Start no later than 9:00 AM to make the most of limited daylight. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula road can be icy and snowy in January - drive carefully and check road.is. Kirkjufell is most photogenic from the Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall viewpoint across the road. This is one of Iceland's most spectacular regions and absolutely worth the long drive.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery day after the long Snæfellsnes drive. Slow morning at resort. Take a beachfront walk and do some journaling or photography review. Visit the nearest town for any grocery restocking needed for the final days of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a deeper cultural exploration. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) - entry around 2,500 ISK but well worth it for comprehensive Icelandic history from settlement to modern day. Alternatively, visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) for local art at similar pricing. Walk through the Grandi harbor district - a trendy repurposed fishing harbor area with street art and interesting architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's famous nightlife area around Laugavegur and Austurstræti streets (bar hopping is expensive but window shopping and atmosphere is free). Visit a local bar for one drink to experience Icelandic nightlife culture (happy hour typically 4-7 PM with cheaper prices). Return to resort. Final dedicated Northern Lights hunting session of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Try Reykjavik's famous Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for budget bites from various vendors (around 1,500-2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort, or Subway/fast food option in Reykjavik for budget dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik happy hour is a great way to experience local bar culture without breaking the budget - alcohol is very expensive in Iceland at regular prices (beer around 1,200-1,500 ISK) but happy hour prices can be significantly lower. The Grandi harbor district has excellent free street art and the Aurora Reykjavik Northern Lights Center museum (around 1,900 ISK) if you want to learn more about the aurora phenomenon.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Iceland. Visit Þórbergssetur (Thorbergssetur) cultural center or explore any remaining local attractions near the resort that you haven't visited yet. Take a final long walk along the Reykjanes Peninsula coastal path, collecting memories and photographs of the dramatic volcanic coastline, lava fields, and winter seascape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Keflavik town center (close to the airport) for any last-minute souvenir shopping. Budget-friendly souvenir options include: Icelandic wool products from thrift stores, locally made chocolate, dried fish (harðfiskur), or Skyr products from the supermarket. Visit the Viking World Museum in Keflavik (around 2,000 ISK) if time and budget allow - houses a full-scale replica Viking ship.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt - this is your last chance. Head to the darkest accessible area near the resort (check aurora forecast first). If KP index is 3 or above and skies are clear, you have an excellent chance of seeing the aurora borealis dancing over the Icelandic sky. Return to resort and begin packing for tomorrow's departure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Budget lunch in Keflavik town - try a local bakery (bakari) for fresh Icelandic bread and pastries (kleina donuts, around 300-500 ISK each).
meals.dinner: Use up remaining groceries from the resort kitchen for a self-catered farewell dinner in Iceland.

day_by_day.notes: Use up any remaining Icelandic Króna (ISK) today as it's difficult to exchange back. Buy groceries, snacks for the flight, or small souvenirs. Pack any perishable Icelandic food items (Skyr, dried fish, chocolate) in your checked luggage. Ensure all gear is clean and dry before packing. Set multiple alarms for tomorrow's early airport check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up early for checkout procedures. Take one last look at the stunning Icelandic landscape from the resort. If there's time before checkout, take a short final walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to Iceland's dramatic scenery. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and head to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 15-45 minutes depending on exact resort location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at least 2-3 hours before your departure flight. Complete check-in, security, and passport control. Browse the duty-free shops for any last-minute affordable Icelandic gifts (duty-free alcohol, chocolate, and cosmetics can be good value). Reflect on 13 incredible days in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Review your Northern Lights photos, geothermal memories, and incredible Icelandic experiences. Begin planning your next budget adventure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast using remaining resort supplies, or grab something at the airport (budget around 1,500-2,000 ISK for airport food).
meals.lunch: Airport food or packed snacks from the resort.
meals.dinner: On the plane or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Budget Summary for 13 days (approximate per person): Accommodation - covered by Aegean Bliss Resort booking. Food - self-catering at Bonus supermarket averages 2,000-3,000 ISK/day, eating out occasionally adds 2,000-4,000 ISK on those days. Attractions - most major sites are free (Thingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss, all waterfalls, lava fields, coastal areas). Paid attractions total approximately 10,000-15,000 ISK for the trip. Transportation - car rental (if split) or bus passes. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation and car: 5,000-8,000 ISK (approximately $35-55 USD) per day is achievable with careful planning.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer or rental car to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind, and get familiar with the property. Keep an eye on the sky during the drive — January nights in Iceland can offer spontaneous northern lights sightings on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack from the hotel or a convenience store near the airport such as Krónan — pick up skyr, bread, and Icelandic cheese for a simple room spread

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is very late — do not over-schedule Day 1. Rest is essential for the days ahead. Download the Veðurstofa (Icelandic Met Office) app and Aurora Forecast app tonight to start monitoring conditions for northern lights hunts.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. After settling in, take a slow orientation walk around the Reykjavik waterfront near the hotel. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church for panoramic city views from the tower (small fee applies). Stroll down Skólavörðustígur street browsing local boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour departing from the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic bites including lamb soup (kjötsúpa), skyr desserts, fermented shark (hákarl) for the brave, and locally brewed craft beer. Visit cultural landmarks including Harpa Concert Hall, the old harbor, and Austurvöllur square with local guides sharing stories of Icelandic history and Viking heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Check the aurora forecast — if KP index is 3 or above and skies are clear, head to a dark coastal area near the hotel for a spontaneous northern lights viewing. If overcast, enjoy dinner at the hotel restaurant and plan ahead for the super jeep tour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Icelandic staples like skyr with berries, rye bread, and smoked salmon
meals.lunch: Included snacks on the food walking tour, or supplement with a bowl of lamb soup at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grillið or Messinn restaurant in Reykjavik — try the pan-fried Arctic char or lamb fillet (~4,500–6,500 ISK per main). Mid-range and highly regarded.

day_by_day.notes: January daylight in Iceland is very limited — roughly 5 to 6 hours from around 11:00 to 16:00. Plan outdoor sightseeing within this window and embrace the long, magical evenings for aurora hunting.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive or guided tour to the Golden Circle — one of Iceland's most iconic routes. Begin at Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament, the Alþingi, established in 930 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area and watch Strokkur erupt every 5 to 10 minutes shooting boiling water up to 30 meters. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall — a powerful two-tiered cascade that partially freezes in winter creating dramatic ice formations. Grab lunch at the Gullfoss Café on-site.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. Stop at a roadside viewpoint away from light pollution to check for the aurora. If conditions are favorable, spend 30 to 60 minutes aurora watching. Return to hotel by 21:00 for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Gullfoss Café — lamb soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate (~2,000–3,000 ISK). Rustic and warming after outdoor exploration.
meals.dinner: Kopar Restaurant near the old harbor in Reykjavik — seafood-focused menu with pan-seared cod and lobster bisque (~5,000–7,000 ISK per main)

day_by_day.notes: Dress in thermal layers, waterproof outer shell, and sturdy boots. The Golden Circle in January can be icy and windswept. A rental car gives flexibility but guided tours are equally comfortable and include transport from Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa for a morning soak — book the Comfort or Premium package in advance as slots sell out weeks ahead. Arrive at opening (07:00 or 08:00 depending on season) to enjoy the milky-blue silica-rich waters before crowds build. Apply the complimentary silica mud mask and algae mask while soaking. The steam rising in cold January air makes this experience particularly ethereal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Upgrade or add on an in-water massage if budget allows (~8,000–12,000 ISK extra). Spend the full afternoon at the lagoon, using the sauna, steam room, and relaxation areas. The Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant inside the facility offers a mid-range dining experience for lunch. Depart by 15:00 and drive back toward Reykjavik.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the hotel after a deeply relaxing spa day. Light evening walk along the Reykjavik beachfront. Check aurora forecast — if promising, take a short drive to Grótta lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes peninsula, a popular and accessible dark sky spot near the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing early for the lagoon
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — fish of the day or Icelandic lamb burger (~4,500–6,000 ISK). Atmospheric dining inside the lava rock building.
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro in Reykjavik — French-Icelandic fusion, known for excellent fish dishes and a cozy atmosphere (~4,000–6,000 ISK per main)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be pre-booked online. Comfort package (~11,000–14,000 ISK) includes towel, one drink, and silica mask. Remove jewelry before entering as the minerals can discolor metals. Hair conditioner is provided — use it generously as silica can dry hair.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast toward Seljalandsfoss waterfall, one of Iceland's most photogenic falls where you can walk behind the cascading curtain of water (may be icy in January — exercise caution). Continue a short distance to the hidden Gljúfrabúi waterfall tucked inside a canyon, accessible by wading through a shallow stream.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall — massive and dramatic, often with ice formations in January. Climb the staircase beside the falls for a panoramic view of the South Coast. Drive further to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík, featuring dramatic basalt column formations, sea stacks called Reynisdrangar, and powerful Atlantic waves. Stay well back from the water — sneaker waves are dangerous here.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in or near Vík village before the dark drive back toward Reykjavik. Keep eyes on the sky during the return journey — the South Coast away from city lights is excellent aurora territory. Stop at a safe pullout if the lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Reykjavik grocery store (Bónus or Krónan) — sandwiches, skyr, fruit, and thermos of hot coffee for roadside eating near the waterfalls
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík village — cozy local restaurant serving lamb stew and fish dishes (~3,500–5,500 ISK per main)

day_by_day.notes: Start early given limited daylight. The South Coast drive is approximately 2.5 hours from Reykjavik one way. Roads in January can be icy — check road.is before departing. Studded tires or 4WD recommended. Reynisfjara beach has claimed lives from rogue waves — maintain a minimum 30-meter distance from the water.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and use the hotel amenities. If the resort has a hot tub or pool, spend time there. Mid-morning, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront near the hotel, watching winter waves and seabirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula, a dramatic volcanic landscape close to the hotel area. Explore the Bridge Between Continents — a symbolic footbridge spanning the fissure between the North American and Eurasian plates. Visit Reykjanesviti lighthouse, Iceland's oldest, perched on dramatic sea cliffs. Explore the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its roaring mud pools and steam vents — a raw and otherworldly geothermal landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Book the Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep departing from Reykjavik this evening. The guide will use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to drive the group to the best viewing location in the wilderness. Super jeep tours can reach highland and coastal areas inaccessible to regular vehicles, maximizing chances of a clear-sky sighting.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café at Reykjanes or packed snacks from the hotel — fish soup to go from a local petrol station bakery is a beloved Icelandic tradition
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the evening super jeep tour — Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik offers premium Icelandic ingredients at mid-to-upper mid-range prices (~5,000–8,000 ISK per main). Alternatively, a quick lamb hot dog (pylsur) from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur kiosk (~600 ISK) is an iconic Reykjavik experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep typically runs 3 to 4 hours and costs approximately 15,000–20,000 ISK per person. Most operators offer a free repeat tour if no lights are seen. Dress in maximum warmth — multiple base layers, fleece mid-layer, and a windproof insulated outer layer. Hand warmers are strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula for a full-day excursion — one of Iceland's most diverse and scenic regions. Stop at Borgarnes town for a quick visit to the Settlement Center museum, which tells the story of Iceland's first Viking settlers through an immersive audio tour (~2,500 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Snæfellsnes and explore the Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano — the setting of Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its ancient lifting stones used to test fishermen's strength. Explore the dramatic Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks and the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi with its natural arch formations and birdlife.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is far from city lights — if aurora activity is forecast, pull over at any dark roadside area on the return drive for a potentially spectacular display. Arrive back at the hotel by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café in Hellnar village on Snæfellsnes — a beloved cliffside café serving homemade soup, bread, and cakes with stunning ocean views (~2,500–3,500 ISK). One of Iceland's most charming lunch spots.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the hotel restaurant upon return, or a bowl of skyr and rye bread from room provisions if arriving very late

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 2 to 2.5 hours from Reykjavik. This is a long driving day — consider an organized tour if you prefer not to drive. The peninsula in January can have severe weather — always check forecasts. The glacier itself is not accessible in winter without a certified glacier guide.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir in the South Iceland highlands — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891. The drive from Reykjavik takes about 1.5 hours. Arrive at opening to enjoy the naturally heated pool (approximately 38–40°C) surrounded by bubbling geothermal springs and small geysers. Far less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon, this experience feels authentically Icelandic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Flúðir area — visit the local greenhouse cooperative that grows tomatoes and cucumbers using geothermal energy, a fascinating example of sustainable Icelandic agriculture. On the return drive, stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake — a striking red and green caldera with a vivid blue-green lake at its center (~400 ISK entrance fee).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by late afternoon. Evening at leisure — explore the Laugavegur shopping street, browse the Kolaportið flea market if open, or visit a local craft beer bar such as Mikkeller & Friends or Kaldi Bar for a taste of Icelandic and Nordic craft brews.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Flúðir village café or packed lunch — the Secret Lagoon has a small café on-site with light snacks and hot drinks (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Ostabúðin (The Cheese Shop) in Reykjavik — a beloved neighborhood bistro with a changing seasonal menu, excellent charcuterie boards, and Icelandic cheese selections (~4,000–6,000 ISK per main)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon admission is approximately 3,200 ISK per adult. Towel rental is available on-site. The pool is outdoors and the steam in cold January air creates a magical atmosphere. Swimwear is required and changing facilities are available. Book ahead as capacity is limited.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park — one of the world's top dive sites and a truly bucket-list experience. The glacial water is exceptionally clear with visibility exceeding 100 meters. Snorkelers float between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in water that is 2–4°C — dry suits are provided and mandatory. The experience is guided and lasts approximately 3 hours total with briefing and gearing up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Warm up after the Silfra experience with a hot drink and dry clothes in the tour operator's base. Return toward Reykjavik stopping at the Þingvellir visitor center to learn more about the geological and historical significance of the site. Arrive back in Reykjavik by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the hotel. Use the hotel hot tub or pool to warm up fully. Check aurora forecast — if conditions are good, take a short drive to Grótta lighthouse or Öskjuhlíð hill in Reykjavik for aurora viewing. If overcast, enjoy a cozy dinner and review photos from the day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the cold water experience
meals.lunch: Þingvellir National Park café or snacks at the tour operator base — hot soup and coffee are particularly welcome after emerging from 2°C glacial water
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic seafood tasting menu or à la carte with Arctic char, langoustine, and monkfish (~5,500–8,000 ISK per main)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling costs approximately 18,000–22,000 ISK per person and must be booked well in advance. Diving requires an advanced open water certification. Snorkeling requires no experience. Do not eat a heavy meal within 2 hours of the experience. Dry suits are provided but bring thermal underlayers — the operators will advise on what to wear underneath.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start — visit the National Museum of Iceland in Reykjavik for a comprehensive journey through Icelandic history from the Viking Age to the present (~2,500 ISK). Afterward, explore the Tjörnin city pond area and the colorful corrugated iron houses of the old Reykjavik neighborhoods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum on Öskjuhlíð hill — a stunning glass dome building housing an artificial ice cave, northern lights planetarium show, and exhibits on Iceland's natural wonders (~3,500–5,500 ISK depending on package). The rooftop observation deck offers 360-degree views over Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains and ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep if the first tour on Day 6 was clouded out, or if you simply want another chance at a spectacular display. January is peak aurora season with long nights. Alternatively, if you had a great sighting on Day 6, spend the evening at a Reykjavik live music venue — Iceland has a world-class music scene. Check what is playing at Harpa Concert Hall.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Perlan inside the Perlan Museum, or Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja for traditional Icelandic rye bread sandwiches with smoked lamb (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hamborgarafabrikkan (The Burger Factory) — Iceland's beloved gourmet burger chain with Icelandic lamb burgers, reindeer burgers, and craft beers (~3,500–5,000 ISK per person). Fun and casual mid-range option.

day_by_day.notes: The Perlan ice cave and northern lights show is a worthwhile indoor alternative on days with poor aurora conditions. Book the second super jeep tour in advance as January tours fill up. If aurora activity was already seen on Day 6, consider swapping the evening for a traditional Icelandic sauna experience at Sundhöll Reykjavíkur public pool.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) via ferry from Landeyjahöfn harbor (approximately 45-minute crossing). The islands were formed by volcanic eruptions and the most recent, Eldfell, erupted in 1973 — burying part of the town under lava. Visit the Eldheimar Museum built around a house excavated from the lava, offering a haunting and fascinating account of the eruption (~2,200 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island town of Heimaey on foot — visit the colorful harbor, the aquarium and natural history museum, and hike up Eldfell volcano for views over the archipelago. The island is home to the world's largest Atlantic puffin colony, though puffins migrate offshore in winter. The rugged volcanic landscape is dramatic and unlike anywhere else in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to the mainland and drive back to the hotel. Arrive by 20:00–21:00. Quiet dinner at the hotel or a simple meal from provisions. Review photos and plan the final days of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Einsi Kaldi restaurant in Heimaey town — casual seafood and Icelandic comfort food with harbor views (~2,500–4,000 ISK per main)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a relaxed dinner without driving back into Reykjavik

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets should be booked in advance at herjolfur.is (~2,400 ISK each way). Check weather and sea conditions before departure as winter crossings can be rough. The ferry does not always run in severe weather — have a backup plan. The Westman Islands are a unique and often overlooked gem of Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — spend the morning at a Reykjavik public geothermal swimming pool for an authentic local experience. Sundhöll Reykjavíkur (city center, historic 1937 pool) or Laugardalslaug (largest outdoor pool complex with hot pots, waterslide, and steam room) are both excellent. Entry is approximately 1,100 ISK and locals use these pools daily year-round regardless of weather. Soak in the hot pots and chat with locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Reykjavik exploration — visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) underground museum built around a Viking longhouse discovered beneath the city (~2,200 ISK). Browse Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs — lopapeysa wool sweaters, lava salt, dried fish, and Icelandic chocolate. Visit Vinbuðin state wine and spirits store to pick up Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) as a gift.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special Reykjavik restaurant. Pack bags and prepare for tomorrow's departure. Set an early alarm. Do one final aurora check before bed — a clear January night sky over the hotel's beachfront location could deliver a magical final memory.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Matur og Drykkur restaurant — innovative traditional Icelandic cuisine reimagined with modern techniques. Try the salted cod head or lamb neck (~4,500–7,000 ISK per main). A memorable culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dill Restaurant — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant offering a Nordic tasting menu showcasing the finest Icelandic ingredients (~18,000–25,000 ISK per person for tasting menu). A splurge-worthy finale for a mid-range trip. Book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: If Dill is outside budget comfort, excellent alternatives for a farewell dinner include Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) or Apotek Kitchen & Bar, both offering high-quality Icelandic cuisine at slightly lower price points (~6,000–9,000 ISK per main). Pack your lopapeysa sweater on top for easy airport access — Keflavik airport is notoriously cold in January.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Enjoy a final hotel breakfast. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Drive to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). If your flight departs in the afternoon, consider a final stop at the Blue Lagoon's Sky Lagoon in Kópavogur — closer to the airport than the Blue Lagoon — for a final geothermal soak before flying (book in advance, ~6,500–9,000 ISK). Alternatively, explore the Viking World Museum near Keflavik (~2,000 ISK) which houses a full-scale replica Viking ship.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik airport with ample time — allow at least 2.5 to 3 hours before international departure. Browse the airport's excellent selection of Icelandic products including Nói Síríus chocolate, dried fish, and geothermal beauty products. Enjoy a final Icelandic lamb soup at the airport café before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland carrying memories of geothermal waters, dancing northern lights, volcanic landscapes, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Keflavik airport café or restaurant — try the fish and chips or lamb soup for a final taste of Iceland (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: On the flight

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank — petrol stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. Allow extra time in winter for potential icy road conditions on the airport drive. Keflavik airport has good shopping and dining but can get crowded — arriving early is always wise. Ensure you have receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over 6,000 ISK — Iceland offers a tourist VAT refund of up to 15% processed at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city lights to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while experiencing Iceland's dramatic dark landscapes.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by black lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel, and one silica mud mask.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (to avoid crowds) or Evening (for potential aurora views in winter)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891. Far less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural setting, offering an authentic local bathing experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local fish markets while learning about Viking heritage and modern Icelandic culture.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the fissure make this one of the world's most unique underwater experiences. Dry suits are provided, making it accessible even in cold temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome glass of Champagne prepared by the concierge, and settle into your beachfront suite. Light late-night room-service supper available.

meals.breakfast: In-flight
meals.lunch: In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort – curated Icelandic cheese & charcuterie board with Skyr mousse and local rye bread, paired with Icelandic craft beer or herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late; keep Day 1 entirely relaxed. Confirm all upcoming bookings with the resort concierge before retiring. January sunrise is around 11:00, so a slow morning tomorrow is perfectly natural.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort restaurant, then a private orientation walk along the beachfront with a local guide to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape. Visit the nearby volcanic shoreline and learn about the geology of the Reykjanes Peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa – Transfer to the iconic milky-blue geothermal lagoon (15 minutes from the resort). Enjoy the premium Retreat Spa package: private changing suite, in-water silica mud mask ritual, floating in 39°C mineral-rich waters, and an in-water massage session with a certified therapist.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring modern New Nordic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Icelandic breakfast spread: smoked salmon, Skyr with berries, freshly baked rye bread, scrambled eggs, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant – À la carte lunch with panoramic lagoon views; try the langoustine soup and slow-cooked lamb
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort fine-dining restaurant – 5-course tasting menu featuring pan-seared Arctic char, reindeer tenderloin, and Icelandic sea urchin bisque; wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance as slots are limited. January daylight is only about 5 hours (11:00–16:00), so afternoon activities will transition into darkness quickly – embrace the atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour – Private chauffeured transfer to Reykjavik city center (45 minutes). Embark on a guided premium food and culture walking tour: visit Hallgrímskirkja church, explore the colorful old harbor district, and sample traditional Icelandic bites including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, kleinur doughnuts, and smoked lamb.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik: browse the Harpa Concert Hall architecture, visit the National Museum of Iceland for cultural context, and enjoy boutique shopping on Laugavegur street for premium Icelandic wool goods and design.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – Depart at dusk (~16:30) with an expert aurora guide in a luxury super jeep. Drive deep into the Reykjanes highlands away from light pollution. Hot chocolate and Icelandic waffles served under the stars while waiting for the aurora borealis display.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Freshly baked pastries, Icelandic yogurt parfait, poached eggs with smoked salmon, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik – Iceland's premier Nordic fine-dining spot; seasonal tasting menu with foraged ingredients (reservation essential)
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik – Traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined in a stylish setting; try the cod's head and lamb heart before the jeep tour departs

day_by_day.notes: Northern lights visibility depends on solar activity (KP index) and cloud cover. The guide monitors forecasts in real time and selects the best viewing location. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00. Dress in thermal layers; the resort can provide gear if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery after the late aurora tour. Enjoy a relaxed brunch at the resort. Afterward, indulge in a private spa treatment at the resort spa – choose from a volcanic hot stone massage or an Icelandic seaweed body wrap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak – Private transfer to Flúðir village (~1.5 hours). Experience Iceland's oldest natural hot spring pool dating to 1891. Far more intimate than the Blue Lagoon, surrounded by geothermal steam vents and a small geyser. Enjoy a private session with exclusive access arranged through the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Scenic drive back through the Golden Circle area at dusk. Stop at Geysir geothermal area for a brief twilight visit to see Strokkur erupt. Return to the resort for a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at resort – Eggs Benedict with smoked Arctic char, avocado, and hollandaise; Icelandic pastries; specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic hamper prepared by resort chef – Artisan sandwiches, Skyr pots, smoked lamb wraps, and thermos of Icelandic lamb soup enjoyed near the Secret Lagoon
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – Slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetable purée, followed by Skyr cheesecake with crowberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon is a wonderful contrast to the Blue Lagoon – rustic, authentic, and uncrowded. The small geyser nearby erupts approximately every 5 minutes. Water temperature is a consistent 38–40°C.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle Full-Day Private Tour (Part 1) – Depart in a private luxury 4x4 at 10:00. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park – a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet above ground. Walk the dramatic rift valley with a private geologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure – At Þingvellir, don a dry suit and snorkel (or dive) in the crystal-clear glacial waters of the Silfra fissure, literally between two tectonic plates. Visibility exceeds 100 meters. Water temperature is 2–4°C but dry suits keep you warm. A truly once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.evening: Continue the Golden Circle: visit the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir and the majestic Gullfoss waterfall (partially frozen in January, spectacularly icy). Return to resort. Optional second Northern Lights hunt if forecast is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Full Icelandic hot breakfast: lamb sausages, black pudding, fried eggs, hash browns, rye toast, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant, Reykholt – Unique dining inside a geothermal tomato greenhouse; tomato soup, tomato beer, and farm-fresh salads
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining restaurant – Pan-seared halibut with beurre blanc, fennel, and caviar; chocolate lava cake with Icelandic sea salt ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires a minimum height/weight and participants must be comfortable in water. Dry suit briefing is provided on-site (~30 minutes). Bring a swimsuit to wear under the dry suit. Gloves and hood are provided. The experience lasts approximately 45 minutes in the water.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast Adventure (Part 1) – Private luxury 4x4 departure at 09:30. Drive the stunning South Coast: first stop is Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can walk behind the curtain of falling water (may be icy in January – guide will advise on safety).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for dramatic photos, then visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara – one of the world's most striking beaches with basalt column formations, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the nearby Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Check in for an optional overnight glamping or luxury farm stay upgrade near Vík (if desired), or return to the resort. If returning, stop at a local geothermal pool (Seljavallalaug) for a twilight soak. Dinner at resort or local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Smoked salmon bagels, cream cheese, capers, Skyr with granola, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant, Vík – Locally sourced fish stew, lamb burger, and Icelandic beer with views of Reynisfjara
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant, Vík – Cozy fine-dining with pan-fried cod, lamb fillet, and homemade Skyr desserts (if staying south); or resort restaurant if returning

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has notoriously dangerous 'sneaker waves' – always maintain a safe distance from the water as instructed by your guide. January conditions can be icy; the private 4x4 and experienced driver are essential for safety on this route.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Experience – Private transfer to Sólheimajökull glacier (an outlet glacier of Mýrdalsjökull). Embark on a premium guided glacier walk with certified mountain guides: crampons, ice axes, and full safety equipment provided. Explore ice caves, crevasses, and blue ice formations up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approximately 2.5 hours further east) – one of Iceland's most breathtaking sights. Watch icebergs calve from the glacier and float serenely in the lagoon. Nearby Diamond Beach features ice chunks washed ashore on black sand, glittering like diamonds.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – The remote eastern location provides exceptional dark skies. Your guide will monitor the KP forecast and position the group at the optimal viewing spot near the glacier lagoon. Return to resort late evening.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from resort – Thermos of coffee, smoked lamb sandwiches, energy bars, and Skyr pots (to-go for early departure)
meals.lunch: Glacier Goose Restaurant near Jökulsárlón – Lobster soup, smoked trout, and fresh-baked bread in a cozy setting
meals.dinner: Hotel Skaftá or Hótel Laki (near Kirkjubæjarklaustur) – Traditional Icelandic dinner: slow-roasted lamb, root vegetables, and fresh berry desserts; or resort dining upon return

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~5–6 hours total driving). Departure should be no later than 08:30. The glacier walk takes approximately 3 hours. Dress in waterproof, windproof layers. The private super jeep can combine the glacier lagoon visit and aurora hunt efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and spa indulgence at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in, enjoy a lavish breakfast, then book a full morning in the resort spa: sauna, steam room, hydrotherapy pool, and a 90-minute signature Icelandic volcanic stone massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private photography workshop with a local Icelandic landscape photographer. Head to the dramatic Reykjanes Peninsula coastline near the resort to capture the unique volcanic landscapes, sea stacks, and geothermal steam vents in the soft winter light (golden hour lasts most of the afternoon in January).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 15:30–16:00) cocktail hour on the resort terrace with panoramic ocean views. Followed by a private chef's table dinner experience at the resort – watch the head chef prepare a bespoke 7-course Icelandic tasting menu at an intimate table in the kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort brunch – Eggs any style, smoked fish platter, fresh-baked pastries, Icelandic waffles with cream and jam, mimosas or fresh juice
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at resort – Grilled langoustine salad, vegetable broth, and Skyr parfait
meals.dinner: Chef's Table at Aegean Bliss Resort – 7-course bespoke tasting menu: amuse-bouche of cod roe, langoustine bisque, Silfra trout tartare, reindeer carpaccio, Arctic char with beurre blanc, Icelandic lamb rack, and Skyr soufflé; premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The chef's table experience should be pre-booked through the concierge upon arrival. Limited to 2–6 guests. The photography workshop can be arranged through the resort or local operators – early afternoon departure around 13:00 to maximize the golden light window.

day_by_day.morning: Snæfellsnes Peninsula Day Tour (Part 1) – Private luxury 4x4 departure at 09:00. Drive north to the mystical Snæfellsnes Peninsula (2.5 hours). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park – the glacier-capped volcano that Jules Verne used as the entrance to the Earth's core in 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the dramatic western tip of the peninsula: the Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks, Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (with the famous lifting stones used by fishermen), and the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi with its stunning cliff walk and arch formations.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Kirkjufell mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall – Iceland's most photographed mountain, especially stunning in winter with snow. Aurora hunt from this iconic location if forecast permits. Dinner in Grundarfjörður before returning to resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Full hot breakfast with Icelandic lamb sausages, eggs, smoked fish, and freshly baked rye bread
meals.lunch: Narfeyrarstofa Restaurant, Stykkishólmur – Award-winning restaurant with fresh scallops, lobster, and seasonal Icelandic produce in a historic harbor setting
meals.dinner: Hotel Framnes Restaurant, Grundarfjörður – Freshly caught fish of the day, lamb stew, and homemade desserts with views of Kirkjufell

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is nicknamed 'Iceland in Miniature' as it showcases nearly every Icelandic landscape type in one peninsula. The round trip is approximately 5–6 hours of driving; an overnight stay in Stykkishólmur can be arranged as an upgrade if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep (dedicated second attempt) – If the aurora was not fully visible on previous nights, this morning begins with a late start (aurora tours run late). Sleep in until 09:30. After breakfast, visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark – explore the Bridge Between Continents (a literal footbridge spanning the tectonic plate boundary), Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools, and the Reykjanes lighthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Krýsuvík-Seltún geothermal area – a colorful, bubbling landscape of sulfurous hot springs, mud pots, and steaming fumaroles in vivid yellows, reds, and oranges. A fascinating contrast to the icy winter surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated premium Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – Depart at 20:00 with a specialist aurora guide. Drive to the darkest accessible location based on real-time cloud and KP forecasts. Hot drinks, blankets, and Icelandic pastries provided. Professional aurora photography guidance included.

meals.breakfast: Late resort breakfast – Freshly baked croissants, smoked salmon, cream cheese, Skyr with blueberries, and specialty Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Duus, Keflavík – Excellent harbor-side restaurant; lobster soup, fish and chips, and fresh catch of the day
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant pre-tour dinner – 3-course meal: langoustine starter, pan-seared cod main, and Skyr crème brûlée; early seating at 18:30 before the aurora tour

day_by_day.notes: January typically has the highest aurora activity of the year due to long nights (18+ hours of darkness). The KP index should be monitored daily via the Icelandic Met Office app. Your guide will have the latest data and will optimize the route accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Cultural Immersion Day – Private transfer to Reykjavik. Morning visit to the Perlan Museum – a stunning glass-domed building with an artificial ice cave, northern lights planetarium show, and exhibitions on Icelandic nature and geology. Excellent for deepening understanding of everything you've experienced.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) – an underground museum built around a Viking-age longhouse. Explore the National Gallery of Iceland for Icelandic art. Stroll through the trendy Grandi harbor district for design shops, artisan galleries, and the Whales of Iceland exhibition.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at one of Reykjavik's top restaurants, followed by optional exploration of Reykjavik's legendary bar and live music scene on Laugavegur and Austurstræti streets.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Eggs Benedict with smoked reindeer, truffle hollandaise, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant, Reykjavik – Famous for cast-iron pan-fried fish dishes; incredibly fresh catch served with brown butter, lemon, and homemade bread
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik – Ultra-exclusive 12-seat counter restaurant (reservation months in advance); avant-garde Icelandic tasting menu with extraordinary creativity and premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Óx is one of Iceland's most exclusive dining experiences – confirm reservation immediately upon booking the trip. If unavailable, excellent alternatives include Geiri Smart or Kopar Restaurant at the old harbor. Reykjavik's nightlife starts late (23:00+) and is vibrant even in January.

day_by_day.morning: Private Helicopter Tour of Iceland's Highlands – Depart from Reykjavik or Keflavík helipad for a breathtaking 2-hour private helicopter flight over the Reykjanes volcanic system, Þingvellir rift valley, Langjökull glacier, and geothermal highlands. Land on the glacier for a champagne toast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a farewell spa afternoon: full-body Icelandic mineral scrub, relaxation in the geothermal pool, and a final beachfront walk to soak in the dramatic volcanic coastline scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gala Dinner at the resort – Reserve the resort's private dining room for an exclusive farewell experience. The head chef prepares a bespoke 8-course celebration of Icelandic cuisine, paired with Icelandic and international wines. Toast to an unforgettable journey.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – Celebratory breakfast: smoked salmon eggs royale, freshly squeezed juices, Icelandic pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light post-helicopter lunch at resort – Charcuterie and cheese board, lobster bisque, and fresh salad
meals.dinner: Private dining room, Aegean Bliss Resort – 8-course farewell tasting menu: oysters with mignonette, langoustine tartare, smoked whale (if ethically sourced and desired), reindeer carpaccio, Silfra trout, Icelandic lamb three ways, artisan cheese course, and Skyr soufflé with crowberry coulis; Champagne and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter tour must be booked well in advance and is weather-dependent; have a backup activity planned (e.g., a private horse riding tour on Icelandic horses, or a visit to the Fontana geothermal baths in Laugarvatn). The farewell dinner is a highlight – inform the resort of any dietary preferences at check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure – Enjoy a slow, indulgent final breakfast at the resort. Take a last walk along the beachfront volcanic shore. Pack and check out at leisure (late checkout can typically be arranged through the concierge for premium guests).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: Optional final visit to the Blue Lagoon for a farewell soak (the lagoon is only 10 minutes from Keflavík Airport, making it ideal for a pre-flight visit). Many guests store luggage at the lagoon and transfer directly to the airport afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of the aurora, hot springs, glaciers, and volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – Full Icelandic spread: smoked fish, Skyr, freshly baked bread, eggs, lamb sausages, and Icelandic coffee; take time to savor every bite
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant (if visiting pre-flight) – Langoustine soup, smoked salmon, and a farewell Icelandic craft beer or sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight – Pack Icelandic snacks purchased during the trip: Nói Síríus chocolate, Skyr, and rye crispbreads for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm exact departure time with your airline and work backward from the airport. Keflavík Airport is approximately 15 minutes from the Blue Lagoon and 45 minutes from Reykjavik. Allow 2.5 hours before departure for international flights. The resort concierge can coordinate all final transfers, luggage handling, and airport lounge access.
